P1.evidence: The setter brief was referenced but not used — 'I spoke with Kim, who set up the meeting. Um, and so he just briefed me in a little bit on your situation, but I must admit, I'm kind of a old school guy and I would like to hear it from you' — so nothing was read back and the prospect was not made to feel seen by it. No frame of any kind was set and no agreement was sought. The open question ran and produced a very long, information-dense answer that contained the entire call in miniature, including the objection that ultimately decided it.

P2.evidence: Injuries were handled well and were the best part of the phase: 'Tell me more about the shoulder injury. What's going on?' produced a forty-year history of four labrum tears and four surgeries, followed by 'Any other limitations in your movements?' and 'So only shoulder is the one that's giving you some headache?' Training week and history also covered properly, including the past-versus-present comparison. Diet asked directly and followed up on processed food. Everything else was missed. Age, height and weight were never asked — weight, body fat and age all arrived unprompted. Work was never asked at all; that he is in medical sales emerged at 00:30:40 as an aside inside an objection, thirty minutes in. Health conditions never asked. Most costly of all, sleep was never asked even after the prospect volunteered it as one of his two limiting factors — 'I'm reasonably sure that diet and probably sleep are the two biggest things' — and the rep did not return to it once.

P3.evidence: The strongest why-probing in the batch, and honest enough to risk the deal. The rep asked the driver question four separate times and refused to accept the surface answer: 'why do you want to do it? Actually? Like, what's the goal?', then 'Okay, but why do you need more muscle? Why?', then 'in your mind, Kerry, like what's the biggest reason actually you want to do this right now?', then 'But is it something that, you know, starts fire under your belly?' and finally the disqualifying statement 'if there is no strong why behind that, I don't know if you need Trevor, actually.' A concrete can't-do-now also surfaced through good follow-up — 'So tell me more about it. What are your plans?' — producing the baseball ambition at 60 and the Hyrox event. Who-else and the legacy drive-through were attempted but had nowhere to go: the prospect's children already regard him as the fittest father they know. No reflect-back was formally run.

P4.evidence: P4c cannot apply here: nothing failed to stick — the prospect has trained continuously for forty years and his current approach is working, which is the whole problem. The rep did get the gap named cleanly with 'What's missing for you right now? Because you're doing a lot, right?... So what's the missing piece for you?' and the prospect answered precisely: 'I'm reasonably sure that diet and probably sleep are the two biggest things.' That answer was then abandoned. Nutrition was presented eight minutes later as something he already does, sleep was never mentioned again, and the one identified gap was never converted into the reason to buy. P4f was also handed over on a plate and dropped: 'there are probably enough workouts online to do things, but like anything else in life, it's always wise to have a coach to kind of manipulate you, help you manipulate things' — the prospect made the argument for coaching himself and the rep replied 'Exactly' rather than building on it.

P5.evidence: Nothing from this phase ran, on the call with the most available material in the batch — a man turning 60 with four shoulder surgeries, a shoulder he is only now able to sleep on, and a stated ambition to throw a baseball again. 'If nothing changes, what does the next two years look like?' asked of that prospect is a different conversation. Instead the consequence question was never posed in any form, so when the price arrived it was measured against peptides and a college fund rather than against decline.

P6.evidence: No belief question and no all-in question. The nearest substitute was an interest question — 'do you feel you would like to follow this kind of approach and take a look into this program?' — and the answer was openly negative: 'It's very interesting. I almost get the impression that it was like, well, we could talk about it, but I don't know if it's really going to benefit as much for what I've got.' That is unresolved hesitation and the script says return to Phase 5. The rep presented the guarantee and the price instead, into a stated doubt about whether the programme would benefit him at all.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. Price was stated, the prospect declined within seconds and without qualification, and the rep moved to a downsell that itself ended in an agreement to receive an email. Payment was never requested and no onboarding step was reached.

objection_plays.detail: No think-about-it, and the prospect explicitly pre-empted one: 'I'm not even going to say, wow, let me think about it.' Worth noting for the corpus — this is a prospect who volunteers that he uses 'let me think about it' as a genuine analysis step on other purchases and chose not to here, which makes the no unusually clean.

Trigger present in substance: 'my wife would think, are you insane? We can put that toward investments or our children's college savings.' No OB move ran. It arrived as justification for a decision already made rather than as a deferral, so running the full play would have been the wrong tool — but the one move that fitted, 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you to your goal?', was never asked, and it is the only question that would have tested whether the wife was the real reason.

The most consequential omission on the call. A clear money objection landed — 'That's way out of line for what I think I can really afford' — and not one OC move ran. No isolation, no HOW-not-SHOULD-I frame, no open-honest-finances request, no financial picture, and critically no payment plan and no financing were offered at all. This is the only sales call in the batch where a prospect stated an affordability constraint and was offered no payment option whatsoever, while Daniel Solano was routed to Klarna, Maz was given four options, Suman was quoted two financed configurations and Tyler was given three. Whether the right answer here was to disqualify is arguable; that the same rep applies the play inconsistently is not.
No timing objection. If anything the prospect argued urgency himself, citing baseball next year at 60.
No fear or doubt about his own execution. His doubt was about the modality's ability to build mass, which is a value question, not a fear one.

Script gap, third and sharpest instance in this batch of 'a cheaper alternative already works for me'. Here the cheaper alternative is free and it is the seller's own content: 'how much more will it get me over just... his workouts that he's posted a bunch of on YouTube. I love his workouts.' He asked it in his opening statement and restated it at the decision point as 'where would my money be better placed for what I can get out of them?' Objection C assumes capacity to pay is the blocker; the blocker here was the marginal value of paid over free, and there is no play, no comparison sheet and no answer. The rep never once articulated what the $4,000 buys that the YouTube channel does not.

Second script gap, and a new one worth logging: the prospect who is already the outcome. 'when you look at his before and after pictures of all his guys, I look nothing like those guys... I'm the after guy, and even better than some of those guys.' The entire offer is framed as a six-month transformation, and there is no positioning for a sub-12%-body-fat 59-year-old who wants refinement rather than change. The rep half-engaged — he had already raised the same doubt himself and to his credit did not pretend otherwise — but the process gives him nothing to sell to this person except a shorter version of the same transformation.

notes: Two things happened here that are worth separating. The discovery was, in one specific respect, the best in the batch: the rep asked the why question four times, refused three surface answers, and was willing to say out loud that the prospect might not need the programme. That is exactly the diligence the offer claims. Everything else leaked — no frame, no work question, no health conditions, no sleep follow-up after the prospect named sleep as a limiting factor, no consequence frame, no commitment check, and a money objection met with no play at all. Coach the two unanswered questions above all: 'will kettlebells actually build muscle for me' was the prospect's opening line and the reason he was on the call, and 'is the windmill a valuable exercise or one to leave alone' for a four-times-repaired shoulder was a safety question. Neither received an answer in thirty-seven minutes.
